The odds ratio of BCG vaccination on COVID-19 severity, controlling for prior medical history count, patients interaction frequency, and their interaction, from a proportional-odds cumulative-logit (logit-link) ordinal regression with the 0–4 severity outcome, is **OR = 1.086 (95% CI 0.793–1.486, p = 0.61)** — i.e., BCG shows no statistically significant association with COVID-19 severity (exp of the BCG coefficient). The model's covariate interaction term (medical-history count × interaction frequency) was positive and significant (β = 0.307, SE 0.122, p = 0.012), but did not alter the null BCG effect (OR 1.09 without it).

Key coefficients (primary model, n = 1000):
- severity(0–4) ~ trt + mh_count + freq + mh_count:freq (proportional-odds logit)
- BCG (exp): 1.0859; β_BCG = 0.0824, SE = 0.1601, p = 0.607
- interaction mh_count×freq: 0.3065 (SE 0.1223, p = 0.012)
- severity counts: {0:803, 1:100, 2:79, 3:11, 4:7}; mh_count (MHORRES=='2') 0–7; freq = patients_seen {1:835, 2:129, 3:36}

Robustness (OR of BCG):
- R1 no interaction term: 1.089
- R2 4-level AEPT severity mapping: 1.106
- R3 MHONGO=='Yes' count: 1.087
- R4 expect_interact binary frequency: 1.063
- R5 BCG×covariate interactions: 1.417 (wide CI 0.60–3.37; model degenerate/unstable — kept covariate-interaction model as primary per plan)

All robustness ORs are close (≈1.06–1.11), so the headline OR ≈ 1.09 is insensitive to the definitional choices; BCG is not significantly associated with COVID-19 severity while the covariate interaction is.
